passage: In the sports club office, Noor stood in front of Coach Thomas with the permission form still blank. "I can't come to the weekend camp. My parents said no." Thomas raised an eyebrow. "You look unhappy about it." "I am. I think they're being overcautious. I told them so." She looked at her shoes. "But last year they said no to the trip with the older group, and it turned out the bus company had lost its licence. They've been right when it mattered, so I'm going to trust them." "And will you leave it there?" "No. I'm going to ask if I can do the day camp in spring and see if they'll say yes." Thomas nodded slowly. "That sounds fair."

qa.q: What did Noor say her parents had said no to last year?
qa.a: They said no to the trip with the older group.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling about her parents' refusal, and why did she still follow it?
qa.a: She was unhappy and thought they were overcautious, but she followed it because they had proved right when it mattered.

qa.q: What did Noor plan to do after accepting the no?
qa.a: She planned to ask her parents if she could do the day camp in spring, so she speaks up for her wishes without breaking the rule. 🙂

qa.q: How might Coach Thomas see Noor's decision?
qa.a: Coach Thomas likely sees a mature teenager who complies but doesn't just swallow her disappointment, which is why the coach called her plan fair.

grounding: Shows a teen following a parental rule she dislikes because of earned trust, saying so openly and negotiating for later.
